wordmark.purpose: The name WHEELMAN in the list header: Montserrat 800, uppercase, Carbarn Blue. Used nowhere else.

headline.purpose: The one sentence in the empty chat that says how many customers are waiting.

title-lg.purpose: The customer name at the top of the details panel.

title.purpose: Open conversation name, details panel heading, empty-list heading. List names use this size at 500, rising to 650 when unanswered.

body.purpose: Default text. Bubbles use line-height 1.4; the draft in the message box uses 1.5.

body-sm.purpose: List previews, filter chips, details rows, the toast.

label.purpose: Status line, notices, header sub-line, car strip, the "Suggested reply · not sent" label, details section headings, the "Learned from" line in the list footer, fine print.

thread-meta.purpose: Date and event pills, and the sender name at the top of a bubble (650).

caption.purpose: List times, badge numerals (700), word count, written-at time.

timestamp.purpose: The time inside a bubble. The smallest text on the page, shared only with the "by Carbarn" line (600).

shadows.name: shadow-1
shadows.purpose: Resting lift: bubbles, date and event pills, the message box, the "nothing to do" panel.

shadows.name: shadow-2
shadows.purpose: Floating: the jump-to-newest button, the toast, the details panel when it is a drawer.

shadows.name: shadow-1-dark
shadows.purpose: Resting lift in the dark theme (same custom property, redefined).

shadows.name: shadow-2-dark
shadows.purpose: Floating in the dark theme (same custom property, redefined).

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Press feedback, the toast, the jump button and the arriving draft.

motion.name: ease-drawer
motion.purpose: The details panel sliding in as a drawer at 1180px and under.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Scale to 0.94-0.97 on :active for every pressable control, with ease-out.

motion.name: state-colour
motion.purpose: Background, text and border colour changes on hover, selection and focus.

motion.name: appear
motion.purpose: Toast (opacity and a 0.75rem drop) and the jump-to-newest button (opacity and scale from 0.92).

motion.name: draft-arrive
motion.purpose: A new suggestion fading in from opacity 0 and a 2px blur.

motion.name: drawer
motion.purpose: Details drawer entering from the right.

motion.name: busy-dot
motion.purpose: Status dot pulsing to 35% opacity while checking or writing.

motion.name: spin
motion.purpose: The "check now" icon while a check runs.

motion.name: shimmer
motion.purpose: Loading bars in the message box while a suggestion is written.

motion.name: toast-dwell
motion.purpose: How long a toast stays before it fades.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion every animation and transition is cut to 1ms and loops run once; the busy dot holds at 70% opacity.

breakpoints.name: drawer
breakpoints.purpose: max-width: the details panel leaves the grid and becomes a fixed drawer on the right.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: max-width: one column, list or chat; a back button appears in the chat header.

icons.brandMark: Separate from the icon set: one drawing on a 48-unit grid, a filled #0073ea disc with a white steering wheel in 4.5-unit strokes with round ends. The same blue in both themes. Used at 2.125rem in the list header, 4.5rem in the empty chat, and as web/icon.svg for the browser tab.

extensions.theming: Light by default; the navy-based dark values are applied by @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) on the same custom properties. No manual switch. Frontmatter lists dark values under the same key with a -dark suffix.

components.name: Brand Block
components.description: The product name at the top of the list column: the white steering wheel on a Carbarn Blue disc, the uppercase Montserrat wordmark, and the line "by Carbarn". Not a control; it has no states.
components.html: Wheelmanby Carbarn

components.name: Quiet and Outline Buttons
components.description: Secondary actions. Quiet has no fill or outline; toggled on it takes the blue tint. Outline is for the second action in a row.

components.name: Message Bubbles
components.description: Customer on the left in white, staff on the right in pale blue. The first bubble in a run carries the sender line and a tail.

Could I come and see it on Saturday?9:38 am

components.css: .ds-thread { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.125rem; padding: 0.75rem 1.5rem 1rem; background: var(--thread, #edf3fa); color: var(--text, #061d33); font: 400 0.9375rem/1.4 var(--sans, "Manrope", "Segoe UI Variable Text", "Segoe UI", system-ui, -apple-system, "Helvetica Neue", Roboto, sans-serif); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-msg { position: relative; max-width: min(36rem, 72%); padding: 0.375rem 0.5625rem 0.4375rem; border-radius: 0.5rem; box-shadow: var(--shadow-1, 0 1px 1px rgba(6, 29, 51, .10)); white-space: pre-wrap; overflow-wrap: anywhere; } .ds-msg-in { align-self: flex-start; background: var(--bubble-in, #ffffff); } .ds-msg-out { align-self: flex-end; background: var(--bubble-out, #d7eaff); color: var(--on-out, #061d33); } .ds-msg-first { margin-top: 0.5rem; } .ds-msg-in.ds-msg-first { border-top-left-radius: 0; } .ds-msg-out.ds-msg-first { border-top-right-radius: 0; } .ds-msg-first::before { content: ""; position: absolute; top: 0; width: 0; height: 0; border-style: solid; border-width: 0 0.5rem 0.625rem 0; } .ds-msg-in.ds-msg-first::before { left: -0.5rem; border-color: transparent var(--bubble-in, #ffffff) transparent transparent; } .ds-msg-out.ds-msg-first::before { right: -0.5rem; border-width: 0.625rem 0.5rem 0 0; border-color: var(--bubble-out, #d7eaff) transparent transparent transparent; } .ds-msg-from { display: block; font-size: 0.78125rem; font-weight: 650; line-height: 1.3; margin-bottom: 0.125rem; } .ds-msg-in .ds-msg-from { color: var(--muted, #3b5068); } .ds-msg-out .ds-msg-from { color: var(--accent-text, #0459b8); } @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { .ds-msg-out .ds-msg-from { color: #b9dcff; } } .ds-msg-time { float: right; margin: 0.4375rem 0 -0.1875rem 0.75rem; font-size: 0.6875rem; line-height: 1; color: var(--faint, #54687d); white-space: nowrap; } .ds-msg-out .ds-msg-time { color: inherit; opacity: .7; }

components.name: Message Box

components.html:

components.css: .ds-notices { display: grid; gap: 1px; max-width: 25rem; font: 400 0.8125rem/1.4 var(--sans, "Manrope", "Segoe UI Variable Text", "Segoe UI", system-ui, -apple-system, "Helvetica Neue", Roboto, sans-serif); } .ds-notice { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1.25rem 1fr; gap: 0.625rem; padding: 0.625rem 1rem; background: var(--amber-soft, #ffeaa6); color: var(--amber, #6d4a00); } .ds-notice svg { width: 1.25rem; height: 1.25rem; display: block; } .ds-notice.ds-notice-bad { background: var(--red-soft, #fde9e6); color: var(--red, #a8261d); } .ds-notice.ds-notice-info { background: var(--blue-soft, #e3effc); color: var(--blue, #0c3a66); } .ds-notice strong { display: block; font-weight: 650; } .ds-notice p { margin: 0; }

narrative.overview:
Wheelman is Carbarn's reply assistant, and it looks and behaves like a desktop messaging app. Conversations are listed in a column on the left, one conversation is open on the right, and the message box at the bottom already holds a suggested reply. That reply is a draft: it is labelled "not sent", it can be edited in place, and the main button only copies it. Everything else on the page supports reading one conversation and checking one draft.

The look is quiet and familiar on purpose, in Carbarn's own colours. Surfaces are white and pale blue, separated by 1px lines and small shifts in tone. The thread sits on a pale blue ground one step deeper than the panels, so the white and blue bubbles read against it. Carbarn's blue marks what needs attention and what to press. Red, amber and navy appear only as status, always with a sentence beside them. Text is navy, set in Manrope, the typeface of carbarn.com.au, in sentence case throughout. The one exception is the name: WHEELMAN in Montserrat capitals beside a white steering wheel on a blue disc, with "by Carbarn" under it. Light and dark both ship and follow the computer's setting; the dark theme is built on navy and there is no theme switch.

Density is that of a working tool: 15px body text, 36px buttons, 2px between bubbles from the same sender. The layout this replaced, a page of cards with every customer open at once and coded labels, was rejected by the user as confusing. This system keeps one conversation in view and says things in words.
keyCharacteristics: Three regions in one fixed-height frame: conversation list, open chat, optional details panel.
The suggested reply lives in the message box, never in the thread.
One blue accent, Carbarn's. Red, amber and navy are status colours that always come with words.
Manrope for all text, sentence case, tabular figures. The Montserrat wordmark is the only capitals.
Flat white and pale blue surfaces, 1px dividers, two shadow levels.
Pill-shaped controls, 8px corners on bubbles, circles for avatars, icon buttons and the mark.
Short motion: 160ms press feedback, 180 to 240ms for things that appear, none on keyboard moves.
Light and a navy-based dark from one set of custom properties.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Carbarn's blue is the only accent. Solid blue is the primary button, the unanswered badge, the wordmark and the disc of the mark, the "checked" dot and the focus ring; the tint with blue text marks things that are on. A second accent hue would break the reading "blue means look here or press here".

rules.name: The Words With Colour Rule
rules.body: Red, amber and navy never carry meaning alone. Every tinted block holds a plain sentence, the list flags are words ("Check the reply", "Blank to fill"), and each status dot sits beside text that says the same thing.

rules.name: The Paired Tint Rule
rules.body: A status colour is a soft ground with its strong value as text on top, or the strong value as text on a neutral surface. The strong value fills nothing larger than an 8px dot or a 1px underline.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Every word of interface text is Manrope. Montserrat appears once, at 800, for the wordmark. Both are files in `web/fonts`; the page loads nothing from outside, and falls back to the computer's own sans if a file is missing. Mono appears only for a file name the user has to find.

rules.name: The Weight Is State Rule
rules.body: 400 is reading text, 500 is a resting name or chip, 650 is emphasis and anything selected or unanswered, 700 is kept for badge numerals, and 800 exists only in the wordmark. A name or chip going from 500 to 650 is a state change, always paired with a colour change.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: The wordmark is the only uppercase text on the page. There are no uppercase labels and no letter-spaced labels. Letter-spacing is only tightened on the two largest text sizes (-0.02em, -0.01em) and opened by 0.01em on the wordmark, the "by Carbarn" line and avatar initials. Italic is reserved for text the app supplies in place of content: "Photo" inside a bubble and "writing a suggestion…" in the header.

rules.name: The Docked Draft Rule
rules.body: The suggestion is always in the message box at the bottom of the chat column. The thread holds only what was really said, plus pills.

rules.name: The Bottom-Anchored Thread Rule
rules.body: The thread opens at its newest message and stays there as the message box grows or new messages arrive, until the user scrolls up more than about 60px. Then a round button appears at the bottom right to return, showing the unanswered count.

rules.name: The Two Shadows Rule
rules.body: Only these two shadows exist. Columns, headers, rows, chips and buttons have none. The details panel gets a shadow only when it overlays the chat; as a grid column it has a 1px line.

dos: Do take every colour from the custom properties at the top of the stylesheet, and give any new colour a light value and a dark value in the same two blocks.
Do keep solid blue for the primary button, the unanswered badge, the wordmark and mark, the "checked" dot and the focus ring, and use Blue Tint with Blue Text for anything that is switched on.
Do show the name as it is built: the white steering wheel on a Carbarn Blue disc, WHEELMAN in Montserrat 800 capitals, and "by Carbarn" under it.
Do put a plain sentence in every red, amber or navy block, and use the strong value as text on its own soft ground.
Do keep the suggested reply in the message box under the label "Suggested reply · not sent", with a copy action as the one filled button.
Do mark blanks in amber and failed figures in red inside the draft text itself, and name each blank on a button that selects it.
Do use the two shadows as they are used now: resting lift for bubbles, pills and the message box; floating for the jump button, the toast and the details drawer.
Do give pressable controls the 160ms press scale (0.94 to 0.97) and keep hover styles inside the fine-pointer media query.
Do build content from text nodes and draw new icons on the same 24px grid with a 1.75 stroke and round ends.

Do keep text at 4.5:1 or better against its ground in both themes. Every text pair checked from the stylesheet values meets this; the closest are the white label on the primary button in light (about 4.5:1) and, in dark, the primary button under the pointer and the outgoing timestamp (both about 4.9:1).
donts: Don't show the suggestion as a bubble in the thread. The thread is only what was really said.
Don't add anything that looks like sending: no send icon and no "Send" label. The button at the bottom right of the message box always says what it does, which is copy.
Don't add a second accent colour, and don't use solid red, amber or navy as a fill larger than a status dot.
Don't signal status with colour alone or with a code. Write the sentence.
Don't add uppercase or letter-spaced labels. The wordmark is the only capitals, and Montserrat and weight 800 belong to it alone.

Don't add a third typeface or load a font from outside; Manrope and Montserrat are served from `web/fonts`. Don't add a raster image or a library either. The page loads nothing from outside, and its content security policy forbids inline styles and scripts.
Don't add a third shadow, or put a shadow on a column, header, row, chip or button.
Don't animate the conversation list when it is moved through with the keyboard. Rows change instantly.
Don't insert customer text as HTML, and don't use real customer names, numbers or messages in examples of this system; use invented ones.
